scenes.headline: How a grammar keeps a model's output in shape
scenes.sub: XGrammar-2's Structural Tags: one schema, many wire formats.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Gumdrop! XGrammar sits under SGLang and vLLM, and stops a model emitting a tool call your program can't parse. Here's how.

scenes.text: Structural Tag separates the schema from the wire syntax: one JSON description, compiled to a grammar that masks the vocabulary at every decode step.
scenes.mark: separates the schema from the wire syntax
scenes.say: The new part: the schema is separate from the wire syntax. One JSON description, compiled to a grammar that masks the vocabulary at every step.

scenes.title: From a tag to a legal token

steps.say: The caller declares a shape: a schema for the arguments, and begin and end markers for the wire format. The engine compiles it to a grammar.
Masks are precomputed into a cache, so at decode time the common case is a lookup.
At every step, a token that would leave the language gets zero probability. The rest are renormalised and sampled.
So there's no decode path to an invalid string. Not ninety-nine percent: a proof.

left.title: JSON-schema decoding
items: The schema and JSON syntax are one thing
DeepSeek V4's XML tool calls don't fit
left.say: A JSON-only decoder ties the schema to JSON. But DeepSeek V4 writes its tool calls as XML, with its own control tokens.

right.title: Structural Tag
items: The schema describes only the arguments
A style picks one of nine wire formats
Triggered tags: free text, then strict
right.say: Structural Tag keeps one schema and adds a style: nine wire formats, one library. Triggered tags let a model reason freely, then call a tool strictly.

scenes.title: Llama-3.2-1B on BFCL-V3, with and without a tag
scenes.note: every recovered point now parses; roughly half of them are wrong
scenes.say: On the smallest Llama, the tag took schema accuracy from twenty-one percent to a hundred. Output accuracy went from five to forty-six and a half.

scenes.text: A grammar guarantees the output parses. It says nothing about whether it's right: that's still the model.
scenes.say: So a grammar's guarantee is unconditional, and narrow. The output always parses. Whether it's right is still up to the model.

recap: A tag compiles to a grammar that masks tokens
Parsing is guaranteed; correctness is not
scenes.say: To recap: a tag becomes a grammar, the grammar masks tokens, and it guarantees parsing, not correctness.
